properties.statement:
THE NUDGE SELF-CHECK REPORTED A PRESENT, WORKING HOOK AS BROKEN WHENEVER ITS PATH WAS HOME-RELATIVE. Reported by flo2 (F1, 2026-08-09) and CONFIRMED IN THE SOURCE rather than from the report: `script_path` in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/nudge.rs resolved `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` and nothing else, so a literal `~/...` was not absolute and fell through to `project.join("~/.local/...")` — a path that can never exist — and every `loop_status` said BROKEN. A shell expands `~` at run time, so the hook itself worked the entire time.

WHY IT IS THE WORST PLACE FOR A FALSE ALARM, which is flo2's framing and is right: this is the one advisory whose entire job is to be trusted when nobody is watching, and it cried wolf about itself. It cost flo2 a real commit (538b460) documenting a problem that did not exist, and it trains a reader to ignore the advisory — the opposite of the lesson.

SCOPE, CORRECTED AFTER ANTHONY PUSHED BACK TWICE, and the correction matters more than the bug. The first framing was 'every consumer following the shipped instructions hits this'. THAT WAS WRONG. The normal install path does NOT produce a tilde: tools/install.sh calls tools/reflow2_install.py, whose `hook_command()` is `python3 "{nudge}"` over a RESOLVED ABSOLUTE Path, and the old code handled that form correctly. So anyone who ran the installer was never affected. The exposed population is those who wire the hook BY HAND from getting-started/AGENTS.md, which documents the `~/.local/share/reflow2/kit/tools/loop_nudge.py` form three times — flo2 did exactly that. The real shape is a DOC-VERSUS-INSTALLER MISMATCH: two shipped surfaces disagreed about the hook's form, and the code only supported the installer's.

ALSO RULED OUT, because Anthony asked directly: it is NOT an artefact of flo2 running against a development build. `git diff v0.26.1..HEAD -- crates/reflow2-mcp/src/nudge.rs` is EMPTY, so the released 0.26.1 binary carries the identical unexpanded `script_path`.

THE FIX, and its direction is deliberate: resolve `~/`, `$HOME/` and `${HOME}/`, and treat anything still unresolved — `~someuser/`, an unknown `$VAR` — as UNKNOWABLE rather than missing, which `status` already reads as Installed. Reporting a working net as broken is the expensive direction; declining to judge a path we cannot resolve is the cheap one. The home directory is passed in rather than read inside, so the tests never mutate a process-wide `HOME` other tests share.

PROVEN BY NEGATIVE CONTROL, not by the tests passing: with only the home-resolution disabled, four of the new tests FAIL — including `a_tilde_path_pointing_at_nothing_is_still_broken`, which is the positive control proving the fix did not simply turn the check into one that approves everything. `the_installers_own_quoted_absolute_form_still_resolves` pins the form that was already working, since that is the one a regression would silently take away.
